review_notes: I read the whole file and the relevant definitions in SpectralOverlapPaths.lean (spectralGroupPath). I also read the downstream uses in CavitySpinObservable.lean and CavityRecalculatedLabels.lean. The file has no simp attributes at all. The two findings come from downstream proofs that unfold these definitions by hand because no unfolding or evaluation lemmas exist. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether the proposed lemmas would close those goals unaided. I did not recommend making any existing lemma @[simp], because the inequalities and Monotone/Continuous statements are not rewrite rules.

findings.excerpt: ⟨cavityCanonicalCoordinate ρ eig hρ hρsum p a t,
findings.problem: cavityCanonicalLabel maps into the subtype Icc (-1) 1 and has no coercion lemma. The only way to see its real value is to unfold the definition. CavitySpinObservable.lean (line 47-48) does exactly this: it adds `cavityCanonicalLabel` to a `simp only` unfold list to expose the coordinate. CavityRecalculatedLabels.lean (lines 49-50) uses a `change` to the coordinate form. Unfolding the definition exposes its proof terms, and an explicit simp lemma would avoid that.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma cavityCanonicalLabel_coe (ρ eig hρ hρsum p a t) : (cavityCanonicalLabel ρ eig hρ hρsum p a t : ℝ) = cavityCanonicalCoordinate ρ eig hρ hρsum p a t := rfl` directly after the definition. It rewrites the coercion into the canonical coordinate form and cannot loop, because the right-hand side contains no label. Callers could then use `simp only [cavityCanonicalLabel_coe]` or plain `simp` instead of unfolding the def or using `change`.
findings.benefit: The label stays opaque, with one canonical normal form (the coordinate) for its real value. The downstream `simp only [..., cavityCanonicalLabel]` and `change` steps become stable rewrites instead of depending on the definition's body.

findings.excerpt: ∫ r in 0..(Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t : ℝ), spectralPathDensity ρ eig hρ hρsum p a r
findings.problem: The coordinate is defined through projIcc, but the file has no lemma that evaluates it on [0,1] or at the endpoint. The only evaluation lemma is the special case `cavityCanonicalCoordinate_at_path` (line 53). Other files must unfold the definition and add `Set.projIcc_of_mem zero_le_one ht` by hand. sum_cavityCanonicalCoordinate does this at line 18. CavityRecalculatedLabels does it at line 46-47 with a hand-built membership proof for 1, and it also unfolds spectralGroupDiagonal. These unfoldings expose the projIcc form, which is not a normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Add `lemma cavityCanonicalCoordinate_of_mem {t} (ht : t ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) 1) : cavityCanonicalCoordinate ρ eig hρ hρsum p a t = ∫ r in 0..t, spectralPathDensity ρ eig hρ hρsum p a r` (proved by `simp only [cavityCanonicalCoordinate, Set.projIcc_of_mem zero_le_one ht]`). Make it @[simp] only if the membership side condition is dischargeable by simp, otherwise keep it as a plain lemma. Also add the endpoint lemma `cavityCanonicalCoordinate p a 1 = spectralGroupDiagonal ...`, which would be a good @[simp] lemma since `1` needs no side condition. Re-derive `cavityCanonicalCoordinate_at_path` from the first lemma.
findings.benefit: The projIcc clamp is hidden behind lemmas, and the canonical coordinate-at-1 form becomes the diagonal. This removes the unfold-then-projIcc_of_mem pattern repeated in downstream files, and `simp` can discharge the endpoint case in CavityRecalculatedLabels.
